entries.reader_content_osis: <div annotateRef="Bible:Hag.2.20" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Hag.2.20" sID="gen91116" type="section"/> <div sID="gen91117" type="x-p"/>The Prophet now proceeds still farther; for there is here a really gratuitous and spiritual promise, by which God affirms that he will have a care for his people to the end. He does not now speak of wine and corn, in order to feed the hungry; but he shows that he would be an eternal Father to that people; for he could not and would not forget the covenant he made with their fathers. There is no doubt but he points out Christ in the person of Zerubbabel, as we shall presently see. So that it is right to distinguish this prophecy from the last; for God has before shown, that the worship which the Jews had for a time disregarded was pleasing to him, as a reward was in readiness, and also that he was offended with the negligence previously reproved, as he had inflicted manifest punishment, not once, nor for a short time, but for many years, and in various ways. What then does follow? In this second prophecy he addresses Zerubbabel, and promises to be a Savior to the people under his authority.<div eID="gen91117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91118" type="x-p"/>With regard to these words, some think that a continued act is signified when he says, I shake the heavens and the earth; and they give this explanation — That though it belongs to me to shake the heaven and the earth, and I am wont to subvert kingdoms, yet I will render firm the sacred kingdom which I have raised among my people. But this view is very frigid: and we see even from this chapter what is meant by the shaking of the heaven and of the earth, of which mention is made. The Apostle also rightly interprets this passage, when he teaches us, that this prophecy properly belongs to the kingdom of Christ. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Heb.12.26">Hebrews 12:26</reference>.) There is therefore no doubt, but that the Prophet means here something special, when he introduces God as saying, Behold, I shake the heavens and the earth. God then does not speak of his ordinary providence, nor simply claim to himself the government of the heaven and of the earth, nor teach us that he raises on high the humble and the low, and also brings down the high and the elevated; but he intimates, that he has some memorable work in contemplation, which, when done, would shake men with fear, and make heaven and earth to tremble. Hence, the Prophet no doubt intended here to lead the Jews to the hope of that redemption, some prelude of which God had then given them; but its fullness could not as yet be seen — nay, it was hid from the view of men: for who could have expected such a renovation of the world as was effected by the coming of Christ? When the Jews found themselves exposed to the wrongs of all men, when so small a number returned, and there was no kingdom and no power, they thought themselves to have been as it were deceived. Hence the Prophet affirms here, that there would be a wonderful work of God, which would shake the heaven and the earth. It is therefore necessary that this should be applied to Christ; for it was, as it were, a new creation of the world, when Christ gathered together the things scattered, as the Apostle says, in the heaven and in the earth. (<reference osisRef="Bible:Col.1.20">Colossians 1:20</reference>.) When he reconciled men to God and to angels, when he conquered the devil and restored life to the dead, when he shone forth with his own righteousness, then indeed God shook the heaven and the earth; and he still shakes them at this day, when the gospel is preached; for he forms anew the children of Adam after his own image. This spiritual regeneration then is such an evidence of God’s power and grace, that he may justly be said to shake the heaven and the earth. The import of the passage is, that it behaved the Jews to form a conception in their minds of something greater than could be seen by their eyes; for their redemption was not yet completed.<div eID="gen91118" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91119" type="x-p"/>Hence he subjoins — <hi type="italic">I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms; I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations; and I will overthrow the chariot and him who sits in it; come down shall the horses and their riders; every one shall fall by the sword of his brother</hi>. He confirms here the former sentence — that nothing would be an hindrance that God should not renew his Church. And rightly he adds this by way of anticipation; for the Jews were surrounded on all sides by inveterate enemies; they had as many enemies as they had neighbors; and they were hated even by the whole world. How then could they emerge into that dignity which was then promised to them, except God overturned the rest of the world? But the Prophet here meets this objection, and briefly shows that God would rather that all the nations should perish, than that his Church should remain in that dishonorable state. We then see that the Prophet here means no other thing then that God would overcome all those impediments, which Satan and the whole world may throw in the way, when it is his purpose to restore his Church.<div eID="gen91119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91120" type="x-p"/>We now perceive the Prophet’s designs, and we also perceive the application of his doctrine. For whenever impediments and difficulties come in our way, calculated to drive us to despair, when we think of the restoration of the Church, this prophecy ought to come to our minds, which shows that it is in God’s power, and that it is his purpose to overturn all the kingdoms of the earth, to break chariots in pieces, to cast down and lay prostrate all riders, rather then to allow them to prevent the restoration of his Church.<div eID="gen91120" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91121" type="x-p"/>But in the last verse the Prophet shows why God would do this — even that Zerubbabel might prosper together with the whole people. Hence he says — <hi type="italic">In that day saith Jehovah, I will take thee, Zerubbabel, and will set thee as a signet, for I have chosen thee</hi>. As we have before said, God addresses Zerubbabel here, that in his person he might testify that he would bless the people whom he intended to gather under that sacred leader; for though Zerubbabel never had a kingdom, nor ever wore a crown, he was yet of the tribe of Judah; and God designed that some spark of that kingdom should exist, which he had raised in the family of David. Since, then, Zerubbabel was at that time a type of Christ, God declares here that he would be to him as a signet — that is, that his dignity would be esteemed by him. This comparison of a signet is found also in other places. It is said in <reference osisRef="Bible:Jer.22.24">Jeremiah 22:24</reference> — “Though this Coniah were a signet on my right hand I would pluck him thence.” But here God says that Zerubbabel would be to him a signet — that is, Thou shalt be with me in high esteem. For a sealing signet is wont to be carefully preserved, as kings seek in this way to secure to themselves the highest authority, so that more trust may be placed in their seal than in the greatest princes. The meaning, then, of the similitude is, that Zerubbabel, though despised by the world, was yet highly esteemed by God. But it is evident that this was never fulfilled in the person of Zerubbabel. It hence follows that it is to be applied to Christ. God, in short, shows, that that people gathered under one head would be accepted by him; for Christ was at length to rise, as it is evident, from the seed of Zerubbabel.<div eID="gen91121" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91122" type="x-p"/>But this reason is to be especially noticed — <hi type="italic">Because I have chosen thee</hi>. For God does not here ascribe excellencies or merits to Zerubbabel, when he says that he would hold him in great esteem; but he attributes this to his own election. If, then, the reason be asked why God had so much exalted Zerubbabel, and bestowed on him favors so illustrious, it can be found in nothing else but in the goodness of God alone. God had made a covenant with David, and promised that his kingdom would be eternal; hence it was that he chose Zerubbabel after the people had returned from exile; and this election was the reason why God exalted Zerubbabel, though his power at that time was but small. We indeed know that he was exposed to the contempt of all nations; but God invites here the attention of the faithful to their election, so that they might hope for more than what the perception of the flesh could conceive or apprehend; for what he has decreed cannot be made void; and in the person of Zerubbabel he had determined to save a chosen people; for from him, as it has been said, Christ was to come.<div eID="gen91122" type="x-p"/><div annotateRef="Bible:Hag.2.20" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen91116" osisID="Hag.2.20" type="section"/><div eID="gen91106"/> <div sID="gen91123"/> <div sID="gen91124" type="x-p"/>Prayer<div eID="gen91124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91125" type="x-p"/>Grant, Almighty God, that as we are still restrained by our earthly cares, and cannot ascend upward to heaven with so much readiness and alacrity as we ought — O grant, that since thou extendest to us daily so liberal a supply for the present life, we may at least learn that thou art our Father, and that we may not at the same time fix our thoughts on these perishable things, but learn to elevate our minds higher, and so make continual advances in thy spiritual service, until at length we come to the full and complete fruition of that blessed and celestial life which thou hast promised to us, and procured for us by the blood of thy only begotten Son. Amen.<div eID="gen91125" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91123"/><div eID="gen90933"/><div eID="gen90750"/> <div sID="gen91126"/> <div sID="gen91127"/> <div sID="gen91128" type="x-p"/>A TRANSLATION of<div eID="gen91128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91129" type="x-p"/>CALVIN’S VERSION of<div eID="gen91129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91130" type="x-p"/>THE BOOK OF HABAKKUK.<div eID="gen91130" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91131"/> <div sID="gen91132" type="x-p"/>chapter 1<div eID="gen91132" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91133" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>the burden which Habakkuk the Prophet saw:<div eID="gen91133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91134" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>How long, Jehovah, shall I cry, And thou wilt not hear? <hi type="italic">And</hi> cry aloud to thee of violence, And thou wilt not save?<div eID="gen91134" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91135" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Why showest thou me iniquity, And makest me to see trouble? And <hi type="italic">why</hi> are violence and plunder in my sight, And he who excites strife and contention? (<hi type="bold">19</hi>)<div eID="gen91135" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91136" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Therefore dissolved is the law, And judgment does not continually go forth; For the wicked surrounds the just, Therefor go forth does perverted judgment. (<hi type="bold">21</hi>)<div eID="gen91136" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91137" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Look ye among the Gentiles and see, And be astonished, be astonished; For a work will I work in your days, Which ye will not believe, though it be told you:<div eID="gen91137" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91138" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>For behold, I will rouse the Chaldeans — A nation bitter and hasty, Which shall march through the breadths of the earth, To possess habitations not its own:<div eID="gen91138" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91139" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Terrible and fearful <hi type="italic">shall it</hi> be, From itself shall its judgment and its dignity proceed:<div eID="gen91139" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91140" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>And swifter than leopards <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> its horses, And fiercer than the evening wolves; And numerous shall be its horsemen; And its horsemen from far shall come, They shall fly as an eagle hastening to devour: (<hi type="bold">30</hi>)<div eID="gen91140" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91141" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>The whole <hi type="italic">of it</hi> for booty shall come; The aspect of their faces will be like the east-wind; And he will gather captives like the sand:<div eID="gen91141" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91142" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>And at kings he will laugh, And princes <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a scorn to him: Every fortress he will scorn, He will gather dust and take it:<div eID="gen91142" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91143" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Then will be change his spirit, And pass through and act impiously, <hi type="italic">Ascribing</hi> this his power to his god. (<hi type="bold">37</hi>)<div eID="gen91143" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91144" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Art not thou, Jehovah, from the beginning, my God? My holy One! we shall not die: Thou, Jehovah, for judgment hast set him; And thou strong One, for correction hast established him.<div eID="gen91144" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91145" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Pure art thou of eyes, so as not to behold evil, And on trouble thou canst not look: — Why lookest thou on transgressors, And takest no notice, when the ungodly devours One more righteous than himself?<div eID="gen91145" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91146" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>Thou makest man like the fish of the sea, Like the reptile, which is without a leader: (<hi type="bold">46</hi>)<div eID="gen91146" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91147" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>The whole by his hook will he draw up, Collect into his drag, and gather into his net; He will therefore rejoice and exult: (<hi type="bold">48</hi>)<div eID="gen91147" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91148" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Hence sacrifice will he to his drag, And incense will he offer to his net; For through them fat <hi type="italic">will be</hi> his portion, And his meat <hi type="italic">will be</hi> rich. —<div eID="gen91148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91149" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Shall he therefore extend his drag, And continue to slay the nations, so as not to spare <hi type="italic">them</hi>?<div eID="gen91149" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91131"/> <div sID="gen91150"/> <div sID="gen91151" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 2<div eID="gen91151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91152" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>On my watch-tower will I stand, And set myself on a citadel; And I will watch to see what he may say to me, And what I may answer to the reproof given me.<div eID="gen91152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91153" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Then answer me did Jehovah and said, Write the vision, and make it plain on tables, That run may he who reads it;<div eID="gen91153" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91154" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>For yet the vision shall be for an appointed time, And will speak at the end, and will not deceive: If it tarry, wait for it; (<hi type="bold">66</hi>) for coming it will come, and will not delay.<div eID="gen91154" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91155" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Behold the elated! not right is his soul within him; But the just, by his faith, shall he live.” (<hi type="bold">72</hi>)<div eID="gen91155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91156" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Yea, truly! as by wine, transgress does the proud man, And he will not rest; (<hi type="bold">87</hi>) For he enlarges as the grave his soul, And is like to death, and is not satisfied; Yea, he collects to himself all nations, And heaps together for himself all the people.<div eID="gen91156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Shall not all these take up against him a parable, And against him an enigmatical taunt, and say, — “Ho! he multiplies what is not his own! how long! And he accumulates on himself thick clay!<div eID="gen91157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91158" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Shall they not suddenly rise up who shall bite thee, And awake, who shall torment thee? And shalt not thou become tramplings to them?<div eID="gen91158" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91159" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>As thou has spoiled many nations, Spoil thee shall all the remnant of the people, On account of men’s blood, and of violence To the land, to the city and to all its inhabitants.<div eID="gen91159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91160" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Ho! he covets an evil covetousness to his house, In order to set on high his nest, That he may keep himself from the hand of evil!<div eID="gen91160" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91161" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Thou hast provided shame for thine own house, By cutting off many nations, And thou hast sinned against thine own soul.”<div eID="gen91161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91162" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>For the stone from the wall shall cry, <note n="154"> <div sID="gen91163" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">Calvin</hi> makes here a change in the discourse; but the whole to the end of the chapter may be viewed as the parable or the taunt mentioned in verse 6, and the particle Ho! may be retained instead of Wo. The taunt seems to have been formed so as to have been especially suitable to be used by the Jews.<div eID="gen91163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91164" type="x-p"/>By regarding the passage in this light, we can understand the sudden change off person in verse 16, if the proposed emendation be disapproved; for we see the same in the former portions of the “taunt.” See 6 and 7, and also 9 and 10. That the reader may see the whole of this passage, containing the “taunt,” in the light in which I am now fully inclined to regard it, it shall be presented to him complete: —<div eID="gen91164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91165" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6. </hi>Will not these, every one of them, Raise up a proverb concerning him, And a taunt, enigmas for him, and say, — “Ho! He increases what is not his! how long! And he accumulates on himself thick clay! —<div eID="gen91165" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91166" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7. </hi>Will they not suddenly rise up — thy biters, And awake — thy tormentors, And thou become booties to them?<div eID="gen91166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91167" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8. </hi>For thou hast spoiled many nation, And spoil thee shall all the remnant of the people, On account of men’s blood, and of violence To the land, to the city, and to all its inhabitants.”<div eID="gen91167" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91168" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9. </hi>“Ho! he has coveted an evil covetousness to his house, To set on high his nest, In order to save himself from the hand of evil! —<div eID="gen91168" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91169" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10. </hi>Thou hast consulted shame to thine house, By cutting off many nations And by sinning against thine own soul:<div eID="gen91169" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91170" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11. </hi>For the stone — from the wall it cries, And the beam — from the woodwork it answers it, —<div eID="gen91170" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91171" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12. </hi>‘Ho! he builds a town by blood, And sets up a city by oppression!’ —<div eID="gen91171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91172" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13. </hi>Shall nothing <hi type="italic">be</hi>, lo! From Jehovah of hosts? Yea, labor shall the people for the fire, And nations — for vanity shall they weary themselves:<div eID="gen91172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91173" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14. </hi>For filled shall be the earth With the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah, Like the waters which spread over the sea.”<div eID="gen91173" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91174" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15. </hi>“Ho! he gives drink to his neighbour! — Thou addest thy bottle and also strong drink, In order to look on their nakedness!<div eID="gen91174" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91175" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16. </hi>Thou hast been filled with reproach rather than with glory: Drink thou also, and be uncovered; Come round to thee shall the cup Of the right hand of Jehovah; And shameful spewing shall be on thy glory:<div eID="gen91175" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91176" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17. </hi>For the violence done to Lebanon — it shall overwhelm thee, And the plunder of beasts — it shall rend thee; On account of men’s blood, and of violence To the land, to the city, and to all its inhabitants.”<div eID="gen91176" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91177" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18. </hi>“What avails the graven image! For its graver — he forms it — Even the molten image and the teacher of falsehood: Yea, trust in it does the former of its form, After having made dumb idols!<div eID="gen91177" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91178" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19. </hi>Ho! he saith to the wood, ‘Arise, Awake;’ To the dumb stone, ‘It will teach?’ Behold it! covered it is with gold and silver, Yet there is no spirit within it! But Jehovah is in his holy temple: Silent at his presence let the whole earth be.”<div eID="gen91178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91179" type="x-p"/>The “taunt” <hi type="italic">may</hi> be deemed as terminating at the end of the 17th verse; but I regard it as continuing to the end of the chapter. The word “neighbour,” in the 15th verse, is a collective singular, meaning every neighbour: hence “their” at the end of the verse. The same may be said of “image” in verse 18, which means every image or images, as “idols” are mentioned afterwards. Such are common instances in the Prophets. “It will teach,” in verse 19, most evidently refers to “the dumb stone” — the idol; for it is expressly called “the teacher of falsehood” in verse 17. — <hi type="italic">Ed</hi><div eID="gen91179" type="x-p"/> </note> And the wood from the chamber shall answer it, —<div eID="gen91162" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91180" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>“Ho! he builds a town by blood, And sets up a city by iniquity!”<div eID="gen91180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91181" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Behold, shall nothing be from Jehovah of hosts? Hence labour shall the people in the fire, And weary themselves in vain;<div eID="gen91181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91182" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>For filled shall be earth with the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah, As the waters cover the sea.<div eID="gen91182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91183" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>Wo to him who gives his friend drink! — Uniting thy heat, thou makes them also to drink, That thou mayest look on their nakedness. (<hi type="bold">112</hi>)<div eID="gen91183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91184" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Thou art filled with shame for the sake of glory; Drink thou also, and be thou uncovered: Poured forth to thee shall be the cup of Jehovah’s right hand, And shameful spewing shall be on thy glory:<div eID="gen91184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91185" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>For overwhelm thee shall the violence done to Lebanon, And the spoiling of beasts, which terrified them; On account of men’s blood, and of violence To the land, to the city, and to all its inhabitants.<div eID="gen91185" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91186" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>What avails the graven image? For graven it hath its framer, <hi type="italic">Even</hi> the molten image and the teacher of falsehood; For trust does the framer in his own work, when he makes dumb idols. (<hi type="bold">122</hi>)<div eID="gen91186" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91187" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Wo to him who saith to wood, “Awake;” <hi type="italic">And</hi> “Arise,” to a dumb stone; — it will teach: Behold, it is covered with gold and silver; And <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no spirit in the midst of it. (<hi type="bold">124</hi>) But Jehovah is in his holy Temple: Silent at his presence let the whole earth be.<div eID="gen91187" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91150"/> <div sID="gen91188"/> <div sID="gen91189" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 3.<div eID="gen91189" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91190" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1</hi> The prayer of Habakkuk the Prophet respecting ignorances:<div eID="gen91190" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91191" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2</hi> Jehovah! I heard thy voice, and was terrified; Jehovah! thy work in the midst of the years, revive it; In the midst of the years, make it know; In wrath thy mercy remember. (<hi type="bold">137</hi>)<div eID="gen91191" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91192" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3</hi> God! from Teman he came; And the holy One from mount Paran: Selah: Cover the heaven did his glory; Of his praise full was the earth:<div eID="gen91192" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91193" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4</hi> And brightness, — as the light it was; Horns, — from his hands they were; (<hi type="bold">143</hi>) And there was the hiding of his strength:<div eID="gen91193" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91194" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5</hi> Before his face walked the pestilence, And come forth did burning coals at his feet:<div eID="gen91194" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91195" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6</hi> He stood, and he measured the earth; He looked, and he dissolved nations; Yea, shattered were perennial mountains, Bent down were hills of antiquity; The ways of ages were his.<div eID="gen91195" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91196" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>For iniquity saw I the tents of Chusan; (<hi type="bold">150</hi>) Tremble did the curtains of the land of Madian.<div eID="gen91196" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91197" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Wert thou angry with rivers, O Jehovah? Was thine indignation against rivers? Was thy wrath against the sea? For thou didst ride on thy horses, Thy chariots <hi type="italic">were</hi> salvation.<div eID="gen91197" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91198" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Quite bare was made thy bow: The oaths to the tribes <hi type="italic">was thy</hi> word: Selah: (155) With rivers didst thou cleave the earth.<div eID="gen91198" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91199" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>See thee did mountains, they fell down; The stream of waters passed away; Utter its voice did the deep, On high did it raise its hands. (<hi type="bold">158</hi>)<div eID="gen91199" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91200" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>The sun <hi type="italic">and</hi> moon stood still <hi type="italic">in their</hi> habitation; At the light of thy arrows did they proceed, At the brightness of the glittering of thy spear. (<hi type="bold">160</hi>)<div eID="gen91200" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91201" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>In wrath didst thou tread on the land, In anger didst thou thresh the nations:<div eID="gen91201" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91202" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Go forth didst thou for the salvation of thy people, For <hi type="italic">their</hi> salvation, with thy Christ: Strike didst thou the head From the house of the wicked, Making bare the foundation even to the neck: (<hi type="bold">164</hi>)<div eID="gen91202" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91203" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>Smite didst thou with his own staffs The head of his villages: They rushed as a whirlwind to drive me away; Their joy was to devour the poor in secret:<div eID="gen91203" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91204" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>A way hast thou made in the sea for thy horses, <hi type="italic">Through</hi> the heap of great waters. (<hi type="bold">168</hi>)<div eID="gen91204" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91205" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>I heard, — and tremble did my bowels, At <hi type="italic">thy</hi> voice quiver did my lips; Enter did rottenness into my bones, And within me I made a great noise; That I might rest in the day of affliction, When he ascends against the people, Who shall cut them off. (<hi type="bold">171</hi>)<div eID="gen91205" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91206" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>For the fig-tree shall not flourish, And no fruit shall be on the vines, Fail shall the produce of the olive, And the fields shall not bring forth food; cut off from the fold shall be the flock, And there shall be no ox in the stalls:<div eID="gen91206" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91207" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>But I — in Jehovah will I exult, I will rejoice in the God of my salvation:<div eID="gen91207" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91208" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Jehovah, the Lord, is my strength; And he will set my feet as those of hinds, And on my high places will he make me to walk — To the leader on my beatings.<div eID="gen91208" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91188"/><div eID="gen91127"/> <div sID="gen91209"/> <div sID="gen91210" type="x-p"/>A TRANSLATION of<div eID="gen91210" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91211" type="x-p"/>CALVIN’S VERSION of<div eID="gen91211" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91212" type="x-p"/>THE BOOK OF ZEPHANIAH.<div eID="gen91212" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91213"/> <div sID="gen91214" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 1<div eID="gen91214" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91215" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>The word of Jehovah, which came to Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah.<div eID="gen91215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91216" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>By removing I will remover all things From the face of the land, saith Jehovah; I will remove man and beast;<div eID="gen91216" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91217" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And I will remove the bird of heaven, And the fishes of the sea: And stumblingblocks shall be to the ungodly! And I will cut off man From the face of the land, saith Jehovah: (<hi type="bold">190</hi>)<div eID="gen91217" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91218" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Yea, I will extend my hand upon Judah, And upon all the inhabitants of Je; And will cut off from this place the remnants of Baal, The name of <hi type="italic">its</hi> worshippers with the priests;<div eID="gen91218" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91219" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And those who worship, On <hi type="italic">their</hi> roofs, the host of heaven; And those who worship and swear by Jehovah, And swear by their own king;<div eID="gen91219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91220" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>And who turn back from following Jehovah, And who seek not Jehovah, And do not inquire of him.<div eID="gen91220" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91221" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Be silent at the presence of the Lord Jehovah! For nigh is the day of Jehovah; Yea, prepared hath Jehovah a sacrifice, He hath prepared his guests:<div eID="gen91221" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91222" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>And it shall be in the day of Jehovah’s sacrifice, That I will visit the princes and the king’s sons, And all who wear foreign apparel;<div eID="gen91222" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91223" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And I will visit all those who dance on the threshold in that day, Who fill the house of their masters By means of rapine and fraud. (<hi type="bold">204</hi>)<div eID="gen91223" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91224" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>And there shall be in that day, saith Jehovah, The voice of crying from the fish-gate, and howling from the second <hi type="italic">gate</hi>, And great breach from the hills. (<hi type="bold">212</hi>)<div eID="gen91224" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91225" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Howl ye, inhabitants of the lower part, For exterminated are the people of traffic, Cut off are all loaded with money.<div eID="gen91225" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91226" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>And it shall be in that day, That I will search Jerusalem with candles, And visit the men, congealed on their lees, Who say in their hearts, — “Good will not Jehovah do, Nor will he do evil:”<div eID="gen91226" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91227" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>And their substance shall be a spoil, And their house a water; And houses shall they build and not inhabit; And plant shall they vineyards, And shall not drink the wine of them.<div eID="gen91227" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91228" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>Nigh is the great day of Jehovah, Nigh and hastening quickly; The voice of Jehovah’s day Will cry out bitterly, — then will he be strong; (<hi type="bold">222</hi>)<div eID="gen91228" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91229" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>A day of wrath <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> that day, A day of distress and of affliction, A day of tumult and of desolation, A day of darkness and of thick darkness, A day of clouds and of mist;<div eID="gen91229" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91230" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>A day of trumpet and of shouting Over the fortified cities And over the lofty citadels.<div eID="gen91230" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91231" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>And I will straiten men, And they shall walk as the blind, Because they have done wickedly against Jehovah; And poured out shall be their blood as dust,<div eID="gen91231" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91232" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>Even their silver and their gold shall not avail To deliver them, in the day of Jehovah’s wrath; And by the fire of his indignation shall their land be consumed; For a consummation, and a speedy one, Will be made of all the inhabitants of the land.<div eID="gen91232" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91213"/> <div sID="gen91233"/> <div sID="gen91234" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 2<div eID="gen91234" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91235" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Gather yourselves, gather, Ye nation, not worthy of being loved;<div eID="gen91235" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91236" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Before the decree brings forth, — (As chaff shall they pass away in a day) Before it comes upon you, The fury of Jehovah’s anger, — Before it comes upon you, The day of the anger of Jehovah. (<hi type="bold">232</hi>)<div eID="gen91236" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91237" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Seek Jehovah all ye meek of the land, who his judgment have sought; Seek righteousness, seek humility, It may be that ye shall be concealed In the day of Jehovah’s anger.<div eID="gen91237" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91238" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>For Gaza, it shall be forsaken, And Ashkelon shall be a waste; Ashod shall they at mid-day drive out, And Ekron shall be rooted up.<div eID="gen91238" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91239" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Ho! the inhabitants of the line of the sea, The nation of the Cherethites! The word of Jehovah is against you; Cannaan! the land of the Philistines! I will also exterminate thee, That there may be no inhabitant:<div eID="gen91239" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91240" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>And the coast of the sea shall be a habitation For sheepcots of shepherds and folds for sheep; (<hi type="bold">242</hi>)<div eID="gen91240" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91241" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>And that coast shall be For the residence of the house of Judah; Among them shall they feed; In the houses of Ashkelon Shall they in the evening lie down; For visit them shall Jehovah their God, and he will restore their captivity.<div eID="gen91241" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91242" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Heard have I the reproach of Moab, And the revilings of the children of Ammon; By which they have upbraided my people; And they have extended themselves over their border: (<hi type="bold">247</hi>)<div eID="gen91242" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91243" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Therefore <hi type="italic">as</hi> I live, Saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, — Surely Moab like Sodom shall be, And the children of Ammon like Gomorrah, A soil for the nettle and a mine for salt, And a waste for ever; The residue of my people shall plunder them, And the remnant of my nation shall possess them.<div eID="gen91243" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91244" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>This shall be to them for their pride; Because they have reproached, And exulted over the people of Jehovah of hosts.<div eID="gen91244" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91245" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Terrible will Jehovah be to them; For he will consume all the gods of the earth, And worship him shall each from his place, All the islands of the nations. —<div eID="gen91245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91246" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Ye also Ethiopians! — Slain by my sword shall they be.<div eID="gen91246" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91247" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>And extend will he his hand to the north, And he will destroy Assyria, And set Nineveh a waste, A desolation like the desert:<div eID="gen91247" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91248" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And lie down within it shall flocks, All the beasts of the nations; Even the bittern and the owl Shall on its pillars pass the night; A voice shall sing in the window, In the door-way there shall be desolation, For he will make bare the cedar.<div eID="gen91248" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91249" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>This is the exulting city! Which sat in confidence, Which said in her heart, — “I am, and there is besides me no other.” How is she become a waste, A resting-place for beasts! Every one who shall pass by Will hiss at her, he will shake his hand.<div eID="gen91249" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91233"/> <div sID="gen91250"/> <div sID="gen91251" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 3<div eID="gen91251" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91252" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Wo to the polluted and the filthy — The city which is an oppressor! (<hi type="bold">261</hi>)<div eID="gen91252" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91253" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>She has not attended to the voice, She has not received correction, In Jehovah has she not trusted, To her God she has not drawn nigh!<div eID="gen91253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91254" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Her princes within her are roaring lions, Her judges, the wolves of the evening; They break not the bones in the morning!<div eID="gen91254" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91255" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Her Prophets are vain, men of deceits; (268) Her Priests have polluted what is holy, They have subverted the law. (<hi type="bold">269</hi>)<div eID="gen91255" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91256" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Jehovah is just in the midst of her, He will not do iniquity; Every morning his judgment He brings to light, — he fails not: Yet the unjust knoweth no shame.<div eID="gen91256" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91257" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>I have cut off nations, Waste have become their citadels, I have destroyed their streets, So that no one passes through; Wasted have become their cities, That there is not a man, not an inhabitant: (<hi type="bold">275</hi>)<div eID="gen91257" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91258" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>I said, “surely, thou wilt fear me, Thou wilt receive instruction;” Then cut off should not be her habitation, However I might have visited her: — (<hi type="bold">279</hi>) Truly! they have hastened, They have corrupted all their doings!<div eID="gen91258" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91259" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Therefore look for me, saith Jehovah, Till the day when I shall rise up for the prey; For my purpose is, To gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, That I may pour upon them my wrath, The whole fury of mine anger; For with the fire of my indignation Shall be devoured the whole earth. (<hi type="bold">281</hi>)<div eID="gen91259" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91260" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>But I will then turn to the people a pure lip, That they may all call on the name of Jehovah, That they may serve him with one consent. (<hi type="bold">283</hi>)<div eID="gen91260" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91261" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Beyond the rivers of Ethiopia shall be my suppliants; The daughter of my dispersed shall bring mine offering.<div eID="gen91261" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91262" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>In that day thou shalt not be ashamed On account of all thy doings, By which thou hast transgressed against me; For then will I remove from the midst of thee Those who rejoice in thy pride, And thou shalt not take pride any more In my holy mountain. (<hi type="bold">292</hi>)<div eID="gen91262" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91263" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>And I will cause to remain in the midst of thee, A people afflicted and poor; And they shall trust in the name of Jehovah.<div eID="gen91263" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91264" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, And they shall not speak falsehood, And not found in their mouth Shall be a deceitful tongue; And they shall feed and lie down, And there shall be none to terrify <hi type="italic">them</hi><div eID="gen91264" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91265" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>Exult thou daughter of Sion, Exult thou Israel; Rejoice, exult with thy whole heart, Thou daughter of je: (<hi type="bold">299</hi>)<div eID="gen91265" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91266" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>Removed has Jehovah thy judgments, He has turned aside thine enemies; The King of Israel, Jehovah, is in the midst of thee, Thou shalt see evil no more.<div eID="gen91266" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91267" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>In that day it shall be said to je, Fear not; Sion! relaxed let not thine hands be.<div eID="gen91267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91268" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Jehovah thy God is in the midst of thee, He is strong, he will save; He will exult over thee with joy, He will rest in his love, (<hi type="bold">304</hi>) He will exult over thee with triumph.<div eID="gen91268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91269" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>The afflicted, at the appointed time, Will I gather, — who shall be of thee; Who sustained for her reproach. (<hi type="bold">308</hi>)<div eID="gen91269" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91270" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Behold, I will destroy all thine oppressors at that time, And I will save the halting, And restore the driven away, To make them a praise and a name In the land of their reproach.<div eID="gen91270" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91271" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>At that time will I restore you, At that time will I gather you; For I will make you a name and a praise Among all the nations of the earth; When I shall restore your captivities, Before your eyes saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen91271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91272" type="x-p"/>end of new translation of zephaniah.<div eID="gen91272" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91250"/><div eID="gen91209"/> <div sID="gen91273"/> <div sID="gen91274" type="x-p"/>A TRANSLATION of<div eID="gen91274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91275" type="x-p"/>CALVIN’S VERSION of<div eID="gen91275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91276" type="x-p"/>THE BOOK OF HAGGAI<div eID="gen91276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91277"/> <div sID="gen91278" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 1<div eID="gen91278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91279" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, came the word of Jehovah by Haggai the Prophet, to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying —<div eID="gen91279" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91280" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, saying — This people say, “The time is not come To build the house of Jehovah.”<div eID="gen91280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91281" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Then came the word of Jehovah, By Haggai, the Prophet, saying —<div eID="gen91281" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91282" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>“Is it time for you To dwell yourselves in your boarded houses, And this house a waste!”<div eID="gen91282" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91283" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And now thus saith Jehovah of hosts, — Apply your heart to your ways:<div eID="gen91283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91284" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Ye have sown much, and brought in little; Ye have eaten, and were not satisfied; Ye have drank, and were not replenished; Ye have clothed yourselves, and were not warmed; And he who gains wages, Gains wages for a perforated bag. (<hi type="bold">330</hi>)<div eID="gen91284" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91285" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, — Apply your heart to your ways;<div eID="gen91285" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91286" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Ascend unto the mountain and bring wood, And build the house; And I will be <hi type="italic">to you</hi> propitious in it, And glorified shall I be, saith Jehovah. (<hi type="bold">333</hi>)<div eID="gen91286" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91287" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Ye have looked for much, but behold little! And ye brought it home, and I blew on it: Why is this? saith Jehovah; On account of my house, because it is waste, And ye run, each of you to his own house.<div eID="gen91287" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91288" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Therefore restrained over you Are the heavens from dew; And the earth from producing is restrained:<div eID="gen91288" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91289" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Yea, I have called for drought On the land and on the mountains, And on the corn and the wine and the oil, And on everything which the earth produces, On man and on beast, And on every labour of the hands. (<hi type="bold">338</hi>)<div eID="gen91289" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91290" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>And Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Josedech, the high priest, and all the residue of the people, attended to the voice of Jehovah, their God, and to the words of Haggai, the Prophet, as Jehovah their God had sent him; and the people feared Jehovah.<div eID="gen91290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91291" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Then said Haggai, the messenger of Jehovah, according to Jehovah’s message, saying to the people, “With you am I,” saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen91291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91292" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And Jehovah stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the people; and the came and carried on the work in the Temple of Jehovah of hosts, their God,<div eID="gen91292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91293" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king. <note n="155"> <div sID="gen91294" type="x-p"/> What is said in a Note in <a href="/ccel/Calvin/comm_vol29.htm|vol29.p347.note">p. 347</a> does not apply to what <hi type="italic">Calvin</hi> says. He refers not, as I inadvertently apprehended, to the present division of the chapter, but to that adopted in the Septuagint; for this verse in that version forms the beginning of the next chapter. — <hi type="italic">Ed</hi>.<div eID="gen91294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91295" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen91295" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen91293" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91277"/> <div sID="gen91296"/> <div sID="gen91297" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 2.<div eID="gen91297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91298" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>In the seventh month, and on the twenty-first day, came the word of Jehovah to Haggai, the Prophet, saying, —<div eID="gen91298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91299" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to all the residue of the people, saying, —<div eID="gen91299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91300" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Who among you is alive, Who saw this house in its former glory, And how do ye see it now? Is it not to that as nothing in your eyes?<div eID="gen91300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91301" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Yet now strong be thou Zerubbabel, saith Jehovah; And strong be all the people of the land; And work, for with you am I, Saith Jehovah of hosts,<div eID="gen91301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91302" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>According to the word I covenanted with you, When ye came forth from Egypt, And my Spirit shall be in the midst of you, fear ye not. (<hi type="bold">354</hi>)<div eID="gen91302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91303" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>For thus saith Jehovah of hosts, — Yet for a little while shall be this,<div eID="gen91303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91304" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>And I will shake the heavens and the earth, Also the sea and the dry land: Yea, I will shake all nations, And come shall the choice things of all nations; And I will fill this house with glory, Saith Jehovah of hosts:<div eID="gen91304" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91305" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Mine the silver and mine the gold, Saith Jehovah of hosts:<div eID="gen91305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91306" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Greater shall be the glory Of this latter house than that of the former, Saith Jehovah of hosts; And in this place will I give peace, Saith Jehovah of hosts.<div eID="gen91306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91307" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>On the twenty-fourth of the ninth <hi type="italic">month</hi>, in the second year of Darius, came the word of Jehovah to Haggai, the Prophet, saying, —<div eID="gen91307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91308" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, Ask the priests respecting the law, saying, —<div eID="gen91308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91309" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>If a man carry holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any eatable, shall it be made holy? And the priests answered and said, No.<div eID="gen91309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91310" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Then said Haggai, If any one polluted in his person touch any of these things, shall it be polluted? The priests answered and said, It shall be polluted.<div eID="gen91310" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91311" type="x-p"/>14 Then answered Haggai, and said, — So is this people, and so is this nation, In my sight, saith Jehovah; And so is every work of their hands, And what they offer, — it is polluted.<div eID="gen91311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91312" type="x-p"/>15 And now I pray, lay it to heart, — From this day and beyond it, Before a stone was laid on a stone In the temple of Jehovah, —<div eID="gen91312" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91313" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Before this time, when one came To a heap of twenty, there were but ten <hi type="italic">measures</hi>, When he came to the vat to draw fifty, There were from the vat but twenty <hi type="italic">vessels</hi>:<div eID="gen91313" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91314" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>I smote you with blasting and mildew and hail, As to every work of you hands; And ye turned not to me, saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen91314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91315" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>Lay it, I pray, to your heart, — From this day and beyond it, From the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, From the day the temple of Jehovah was founded; — Lay it to your heart, —<div eID="gen91315" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91316" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Is there now seed in the barn? And as yet the vine and the fig tree, And the pomegranate and the olive, Have produced nothing; — From this day will I bless you. (<hi type="bold">378</hi>)<div eID="gen91316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91317" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>And the word of Jehovah came again to Haggai, on the twenty-fourth of the month, saying, —<div eID="gen91317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91318" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>Speak to Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, saying, —<div eID="gen91318" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91319" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>I will shake the heavens and the earth, And will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, And destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations; Yea, I will overthrow chariots and their riders, And down shall come the horses and their riders, Every one by the sword of his brother:<div eID="gen91319" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91320" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>In that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, I will take the Zerubbabel, The son of Shealtiel, my servant, saith Jehovah, And I will make thee as a signet, For I have chosen thee, saith Jehovah of hosts.<div eID="gen91320" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen91296"/><div eID="gen91273"/><div eID="gen91126"/> <div sID="gen91321"/>
